sources.title: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults
sources.population: Healthy adults; resistance training interventions of at least six weeks
sources.supports: Progressive resistance training improves muscle function; goals and response guide prescription.
sources.limitations: Does not establish an individually optimal split, RIR target, progression increment, or mandatory periodization. Not rehabilitation.
sources.access_scope: PubMed abstract; publisher summary; full-text retrieval was unavailable

sources.title: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
sources.population: Adults, with separate recommendations for specific populations
sources.supports: Adult population guidance includes aerobic activity and muscle strengthening.
sources.limitations: Population targets are not a starting prescription for every person.

sources.title: WHO Healthy diet
sources.supports: Dietary adequacy, diversity, fruit/vegetables and fibre matter beyond macro totals.
sources.limitations: Does not establish personalized energy or sports-nutrition targets.

sources.title: International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise
sources.supports: Provides a commonly used 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day protein range for exercising adults.
sources.limitations: Not a mandatory minimum for everyone; clinical and body-size context matter.

sources.title: Protein supplementation and resistance-training adaptations: systematic review and meta-regression
sources.population: Healthy adults undertaking prolonged resistance training
sources.supports: Supports adequate protein alongside resistance training, with diminishing average gains at higher intakes.
sources.limitations: The estimated breakpoint is uncertain and is not an individual ceiling or proof that supplementation is necessary.

sources.title: A new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure in healthy individuals
sources.population: 498 healthy subjects aged 19–78, including normal-weight and obese adults
sources.supports: Estimates resting energy from body mass, height, age and an equation coefficient.
sources.limitations: Predictive error and population limits apply; not total expenditure or a calorie prescription.

sources.title: Quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on bodyweight
sources.supports: Weight responses to changed intake are dynamic.
sources.limitations: Does not validate converting one week of scale change into an exact energy deficit.

sources.title: Accuracy in Predicting Repetitions to Task Failure in Resistance Exercise
sources.population: Participants estimating repetitions to task failure in resistance exercise
sources.supports: RIR estimates contain error and vary with the exercise and proximity to failure.
sources.limitations: Self-reported effort is not an objective measurement; do not force failure testing to calibrate it.

sources.title: WHO STEPS: Part 3, Section 5, physical measurements
sources.supports: Defines repeatable height, weight and waist measurement methods.
sources.limitations: Self-measurement adds error; circumference is not body-fat percentage or a diagnosis.

sources.title: NHS: How to record your weight
sources.supports: Use consistent scales, placement, timing and clothing for repeatability.
sources.limitations: The programme recommends weekly-to-monthly intervals; frequent weighing is optional, not universally better.

sources.title: USDA FoodData Central Foundation Foods Documentation
sources.population: Laboratory and compiled food composition records
sources.supports: Describes food composition, portion calculations, and general versus specific Atwater energy factors.
sources.limitations: Averages and label rounding do not provide exact metabolizable energy for an individual meal/person.

sources.title: IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport
sources.population: Athletes with possible problematic low energy availability
sources.supports: Under-fuelling can affect health and performance; concerning patterns need qualified assessment.
sources.limitations: Symptoms are not diagnostic by themselves; the toolkit does not implement a clinical REDs score.

sources.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult
sources.supports: Regularly obtaining at least seven hours is the general adult recommendation in this consensus.
sources.limitations: Individual needs differ; hours alone do not establish sleep quality or explain fatigue.

sources.title: Dietary Supplements for Exercise and Athletic Performance
sources.supports: Ingredient-specific benefits and safety vary; adequate diet and training remain foundational.
sources.limitations: Check the actual ingredient, dose, interactions, product and current evidence before recommending.
